messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: lavaan wih RDS
parts: I was wondering how we can use lavaan package for mediation in Respondent driving sampling where we have weights and reference ID.??

I only learned that term when you posted it.  I am unfamiliar with how the weights are applied.  If the calculation of RDS weights allows them to be treated as normal sampling weights, then you can pass that variable name to lavaan's sampling.weights= argument.  If the "reference ID" variable indicates who knows whom in the snowball sampling, I doubt that can be treated as independent clusters using lavaan's cluster= argument because connections among individuals are more like an interpersonal network.  Maybe some solution similar to how spatial dependency is handled?  Not sure; again, I only just heard of the RDS approach to "cure" the ills of snowball sampling.  Sounds clever, but I doubt the lavaan package can accommodate it.

Terrence D. Jorgensen
Assistant Professor, Methods and Statistics
Research Institute for Child Development and Education, the University of Amsterdam
http://www.uva.nl/profile/t.d.jorgensen

messages.author: b8fd92e5e3662745
messages.subject: Re: lavaan wih RDS
parts:
RDS has its own set of diagnostics of how much you can trust the statistical results -- roughly speaking, the recruitment chain must forget its initial (often very nonrandom) starting point, much like you'd have to burnin with MCMC. If all recruitment chains are of length 3, then the results are going to be crap no matter how hard you pretend they aren't.

As far as GEE models go, you can probably fake the spatial correlations by feeding the "neighbor" / connection matrices. Although frankly I don't know if that is properly supported by any R packages -- see if anything under "Spatial regression" under https://cran.rstudio.com/web/views/Spatial.html could work.
